title: Attosecond Path Qubits in High-Harmonic Generation: Classical Dephasing and Trace-Out Decoherence
authors: A. Marchisio, C. Granados, M. F. Ciappina, O. Cohen
abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) is governed by interference between electron trajectories. We propose that the dominant short and long trajectories define an experimentally addressable two-level subsystem: an attosecond path qubit (APQ). We formulate a trajectory-resolved density matrix to identify two distinct coherence-loss mechanisms: classical dephasing from ensemble averaging and quantum decoherence arising from the trace-out of unobserved degrees of freedom. By investigating shot-to-shot fluctuations and unresolved transverse momentum, we demonstrate that while dephasing suppresses coherence through averaging, the ``trace-out'' channel produces mixed states even for fixed driving parameters. We explore how these mechanisms modify APQ purity and show that mode selection and conditioning provide operational routes to isolate them. These results establish a reduced-state framework for diagnosing coherence loss in HHG and for engineering trajectory-based quantum states in attosecond interferometry.
summary: The paper treats High-Harmonic Generation as a form of attosecond interferometry, defining the two dominant electron paths (short and long) as an Attosecond Path Qubit (APQ). It rigorously distinguishes between decoherence caused by classical laser intensity fluctuations (dephasing) and fundamental information loss due to unobserved transverse momentum (trace-out). This establishes HHG as a powerful tool for quantum state characterization in the attosecond regime.
main_problem: To develop a reduced-state framework for diagnosing coherence loss in High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) by treating the dominant short and long electron trajectories as an experimentally addressable two-level subsystem: an attosecond path qubit (APQ).
main_result: The study successfully distinguishes between classical dephasing (ensemble averaging) and fundamental quantum decoherence (trace-out of unobserved transverse momentum), establishing HHG as a platform for engineering trajectory-based quantum states.
method: The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved density matrix for the APQ, analyzing its evolution under both environmental coupling models: classical noise and partial tracing over transverse degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The physical system is High-Harmonic Generation (HHG), modeled using the Strong-Field Approximation (SFA). The core concept involves mapping the electron's continuum dynamics onto an effective two-level Hilbert space spanned by short and long quantum trajectories, forming the APQ.
key_observables: APQ purity ($	ext{Tr}[ho^2]$), Bloch vector components ($r_x, r_y, r_z$), Interferometric Visibility ($V$), and Predictability ($P$).
important_parameters: Attosecond timescale dynamics, laser intensity fluctuations (Gaussian distribution), transverse momentum integration limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Strong-Field Approximation (SFA) and assumes that short and long trajectories define an approximately orthogonal basis for the APQ.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Bloch vector dynamics for both pure states and mixed states under dephasing (intensity fluctuations) and decoherence (transverse momentum integration), showing the reduction of coherence magnitude in both cases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the APQ basis from HHG trajectories, then quantifying coherence loss via two distinct channels—classical dephasing and quantum trace-out decoherence—to establish a comprehensive diagnostic framework for attosecond interferometry.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges attosecond physics (HHG) with fundamental concepts of open quantum systems theory, providing measurable signatures ($V$ vs. $P$) to diagnose coherence loss in an extreme non-equilibrium quantum process.
